threads.body:
@copilot Update this PR directly to confine empty-to-null conversion to the RocketMQ API boundaries. The user asked which RocketMQ getters return empty strings and whether we can convert only at those reads, then explicitly requested cloud implementation of this approach.

The verified upstream APIs are org.apache.rocketmq.client.java.message.protocol.Resource.getNamespace(), whose name-only constructor sets StringUtils.EMPTY, and the generated apache.rocketmq.v2.Resource.getResourceNamespace(), whose proto3 string defaults to empty. Sources for the supported 5.0.0 baseline are https://github.com/apache/rocketmq-clients/blob/rocketmq-client-java-5.0.0/java/client/src/main/java/org/apache/rocketmq/client/java/message/protocol/Resource.java and https://github.com/apache/rocketmq-clients/blob/rocketmq-client-java-5.0.0/cpp/proto/apache/rocketmq/v2/definition.proto . The 5.0.2 Resource implementation used by existing tests has the same behavior.

In RocketMqReceiveRequest.create(String consumerGroup, List<MessageView> messages), apply StringUtils.emptyToNull immediately to the namespace obtained from ((MessageViewImpl) message).getMessageQueue().getTopicResource().getNamespace(), before storing it in our request. In getNamespace(), return the stored nullable namespace unchanged when request == null; apply StringUtils.emptyToNull only to request.getMessageQueue().getTopic().getResourceNamespace() in the protobuf-request branch. Remove the conversion around the combined result. Preserve nullable contracts and avoid redundant reconversion of an already-normalized internal field.

ProducerImplInstrumentation and RocketMqConsumerProcessAttributeExtractor already convert immediately at their Resource.getNamespace() reads. Preserve those boundaries and the producer's outer messageQueues.isEmpty() ternary. Keep the module-local generic StringUtils.emptyToNull helper and its behavior unchanged: null or empty becomes null, nonempty strings including whitespace remain unchanged. Do not instrument or modify RocketMQ's own getter implementations.

Keep all other production fixes, configured namespace behavior, Cassandra batch/query behavior, and previous assertion cleanup unchanged. The user does not want new tests: do not add test methods, test classes, suites, build wiring, or replacement absence checks. Use existing relevant RocketMQ regression/integration tests and run the narrowest applicable spotlessApply task directly before validation. Keep this PR a draft and update its existing branch, not another PR. Do not resolve review threads. The previous coding attempt and its clean latest-head review have completed; this is a user-directed behavior-preserving boundary cleanup.
